cases.question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.standalone_question: What are the three main topic areas covered in COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics?
cases.answer_excerpt:
COMP 1113 Applied Mathematics covers three core topic areas designed to build a foundation for programming and technical courses:

* **Boolean algebra and logic circuit design:** Explores truth tables, Boolean expressions, canonical forms, Karnaugh maps, and designing logic circuits such as adders and decoders.
* **Number systems and data representation:** Covers positional number systems, base conversions, arithmetic operations in various bases, and how computers represent numbers, text, and graphics (including floating-point representation).
* **Functions, linear equations, vectors, and matrices:** Examines systems of linear equations, matrix operations, determinants, and an introduction to functions and Big O notation.

cases.question: Three quick questions: is peer tutoring free, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.standalone_question: Is peer tutoring free at BCIT, can I opt out of the BCITSA health and dental plan, and what student residences are on the Burnaby campus?
cases.answer_excerpt:
Yes, BCIT peer tutoring is completely free for all students, you can opt out of the student health and dental plan within 30 days of your program starting if you already have comparable coverage, and the Burnaby campus offers both the newly opened Tall Timber Student Housing and legacy townhouses.

* **Peer Tutoring:** Peer tutoring is a free service available to all BCIT students on a drop-in basis without needing advance registration. 
* **Health and Dental Plan Opt-Out:** Full-time eligible students in programs running for 16 weeks or longer are automatically covered by the BCITSA Student Health and Dental Plan. If you already have comparable extended health and dental benefits, you can opt out within 30 days from the start of your program (once per 12 months). Note that after this deadline, opt-outs cannot be processed.
* **Burnaby Campus Residences:** BCIT provides over 800 rooms on the Burnaby Campus. This includes the 12-storey Tall Timber Student Housing building (opened in Summer/Fall 2025 with studio rooms, connected single rooms, and priority access for certain groups) as well as legacy townhouses that host 12 students each in private rooms with shared common facilities.
